## [AcceptAgreementCancellationRequest](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_AcceptAgreementCancellationRequest.html)

Allows buyers (acceptors) to accept a cancellation request that is in `PENDING_APPROVAL` status. Once accepted, the cancellation request transitions to `APPROVED` status and the agreement cancellation will be processed.

## [AcceptAgreementPaymentRequest](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_AcceptAgreementPaymentRequest.html)

Allows buyers (acceptors) to accept a payment request that is in `PENDING_APPROVAL` status. Once accepted, the payment request transitions to `APPROVED` status and the charge will be processed. Buyers can optionally provide a purchase order reference for their internal tracking.

## [AcceptAgreementRequest](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_AcceptAgreementRequest.html)

Accepts an agreement request to finalize the agreement. The acceptor can optionally provide purchase orders to associate with the agreement charges.

## [CancelAgreement](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_CancelAgreement.html)

Allows an acceptor to cancel an active agreement. Not all agreements are eligible for cancellation. Use the error response to determine why a cancellation request was rejected.

response.name: CancelAgreement-400

request.description: ## [CreateAgreementRequest](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_CreateAgreementRequest.html) Creates an agreement request that acts as a quote for the terms you want to accept. The agreement request captures the requested terms, calculates charges, and returns a summary. Use `AcceptAgreementRequest` with the returned `agreementRequestId` to finalize the agreement. In the request payload: - `agreementProposalIdentifier` — the `agreementProposalId` from the [GetOffer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-discovery_GetOffer.html) response. - `requestedTerms` — constructed from the terms in the [GetOfferTerms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-discovery_GetOfferTerms.html) response. Each term requires its `id`, and some require additional `configuration`. See [Constructing requestedTerms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/work-with-agreement-api-buyer.html#car-requested-term-overview). See [Working with Agreement](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/work-with-agreement-api-buyer.html#buyer-generate-quote) documenation for more details.

## [DescribeAgreement](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_DescribeAgreement.html)

Provides details about an agreement, such as the proposer, acceptor, start date, and end date.

## [GetAgreementCancellationRequest](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_GetAgreementCancellationRequest.html)

Retrieves detailed information about a specific agreement cancellation request. Both sellers (proposers) and buyers (acceptors) can use this operation to view cancellation requests associated with their agreements.

## [GetAgreementEntitlements](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_GetAgreementEntitlements.html)

Acceptor can obtain agreement level view of status and details of entitlements tied to their agreement - for example, whether it's in the process of being granted or if it has been rejected (and if so, for what reasons), what's the entitlements being granted to customers.

Use `GetAgreementEntitlements` to obtain a registration token. This short-lived token (valid for 30 minutes) is required by acceptors to set up an account with proposers. Currently only applicable for SaaS purchase agreements.

## [GetAgreementPaymentRequest](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_GetAgreementPaymentRequest.html)

Retrieves detailed information about a specific payment request. Both sellers (proposers) and buyers (acceptors) can use this operation to view payment requests associated with their agreements. The response includes the current status, charge details, timestamps, and the charge ID if the request has been approved.

## [GetAgreementTerms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_GetAgreementTerms.html)

Obtains details about the terms in an agreement that you participated in as proposer or acceptor.

The details include:

- `TermType` – The type of term, such as `LegalTerm`, `RenewalTerm`, or `ConfigurableUpfrontPricingTerm`.
    
- `TermID` – The ID of the particular term, which is common between offer and agreement.
    
- `TermPayload` – The key information contained in the term, such as the EULA for `LegalTerm` or pricing and dimensions for various pricing terms, such as `ConfigurableUpfrontPricingTerm` or `UsageBasedPricingTerm`.
    
- `Configuration` – The buyer/acceptor's selection at the time of agreement creation, such as the number of units purchased for a dimension or setting the `EnableAutoRenew` flag.

## [ListAgreementCancellationRequests](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_ListAgreementCancellationRequests.html)

Lists agreement cancellation requests available to you as a seller or buyer. Both sellers (proposers) and buyers (acceptors) can use this operation to find cancellation requests by specifying their party type and applying optional filters.

## [ListAgreementCharges](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_ListAgreementCharges.html)

Allows acceptors to view charges and purchase orders that are associated with an agreement. The response includes details about all charges regardless of whether a purchase order is linked to each charge.

## [ListAgreementPaymentRequests](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_ListAgreementPaymentRequests.html)

Lists payment requests available to you as a seller or buyer. Both sellers (proposers) and buyers (acceptors) can use this operation to find payment requests by specifying their party type and applying optional parameters.

## [RejectAgreementCancellationRequest](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_RejectAgreementCancellationRequest.html)

Allows buyers (acceptors) to reject a cancellation request that is in `PENDING_APPROVAL` status. Once rejected, the cancellation request transitions to `REJECTED` status and the agreement remains active. Buyers must provide a reason for the rejection.

## [RejectAgreementPaymentRequest](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_RejectAgreementPaymentRequest.html)

Allows buyers (acceptors) to reject a payment request that is in `PENDING_APPROVAL` status. Once rejected, the payment request transitions to `REJECTED` status and cannot be accepted. Buyers can optionally provide a reason for the rejection.

## [SearchAgreements](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_SearchAgreements.html)

Acceptor can perform search across all agreements that they participated in as acceptor in AWS Marketplace. The search returns a list of agreements with basic agreement information.

## [UpdatePurchaseOrders](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_UpdatePurchaseOrders.html)

Allows buyers to associate a purchase order with an agreement's charges after an agreement is created.

item.description:
## SaaS Private Offer Procurement

Buyer journey to accept a SaaS offer with pricing terms **ConfigurableUpfrontPricingTerm + Flexible Payment Schedule**.

**Flow**: Setup → Discover → Subscribe → Activate → Verify

---

### Phase 1 — Discover

The buyer discovers and inspects the private offer:

- **GetOffer** — Discover the private offer via the Discovery API
    
- **GetOfferTerms** — Retrieve offer terms including pricing and flexible payment schedule
    

---

### Phase 2 — Subscribe

The buyer initiates and accepts the agreement:

- **CreateAgreementRequest** — Initiate the agreement/subscription via the Agreement API
    
- **AcceptAgreementRequest_with_purchase_order** — Accept the agreement with a Purchase Order
    
- **ListAgreementPaymentRequests** — List the payment schedule requests associated with the agreement
    
- **UpdatePurchaseOrders** — Update purchase order details as needed
    

---

### Phase 3 — Activate

The goal of this phase is to obtain the SaaS vendor fulfillment URL and registration token needed to register the buyer with the SaaS vendor:

- **ListFulfillmentOptions** — Returns the `fulfillmentUrl` (base SaaS vendor redirect URL) via the Discovery API
    
- **GetAgreementEntitlements** — Returns the registration token from the Agreement API. Its post-response script saves the base `fulfillmentUrl` as the collection variable `sellerRegistrationUrl` and the token as `registrationToken`.
    

Note: The registration token must be sent as form data, not as a query parameter. See the AWS Marketplace SaaS product customer setup guide: [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/userguide/saas-product-customer-setup.html](https://null)

Real-world scenario: In a live integration, the buyer's browser completes registration by auto-submitting an HTML form (POST) to the `fulfillmentUrl` with `x-amzn-marketplace-token` set to the plain registration token (and `x-amzn-marketplace-offer-type=free-trial` when the offer is a free trial). The buyer then lands on the SaaS vendor's registration page to finish setup within their authenticated session. The Postman collection stops at preparing these values, since the form POST and the buyer's session belong to the browser, not the API client.

Optional — validate form-data acceptance (testing only): To confirm the fulfillment endpoint accepts the token as form data, you can POST it from a post-response script. This only checks endpoint/format behavior — it does not open a browser, carry a buyer session, or complete registration.

```
const token = pm.collectionVariables.get("registrationToken");
const fulfillmentUrl = pm.collectionVariables.get("fulfillmentUrl");
const formData = [{ key: "x-amzn-marketplace-token", value: token }];
// Free-trial offers only:
// formData.push({ key: "x-amzn-marketplace-offer-type", value: "free-trial" });
pm.sendRequest({
    url: fulfillmentUrl,
    method: "POST",
    header: { "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" },
    body: { mode: "urlencoded", urlencoded: formData }
}, (err, res) => {
    console.log(err ? `POST failed: ${err}` : `POST status: ${res.code}`);
});

 ```

For reference, the equivalent browser handoff that actually registers the buyer:

```
<form id="mp" method="POST" action="FULFILLMENT_URL">
  <input type="hidden" name="x-amzn-marketplace-token" value="TOKEN">
  <comment class='preserveHtml' class='preserveHtml'> free trial only  -->
  <input type="hidden" name="x-amzn-marketplace-offer-type" value="free-trial">
</form>
<script>document.getElementById('mp').submit();</script>

 ```

### Phase 4 — Verify

The buyer verifies the agreement is fully in place:

- **SearchAgreements-product** — Verify the agreement exists for the product
    
- **DescribeAgreement** — Get full agreement details
    
- **GetAgreementTerms** — Retrieve the final agreement terms
    
- **ListAgreementCharges** — Review all charges associated with the agreement

# Buyer journey to purchase annual pricing model for AMI product

## Overview

This folder contains requests for testing **AMI product workflows** with **Configurable Upfront Pricing Terms** on AWS Marketplace.

## ⚠️ Key Concept: AMI Annual Pricing Creates 2 Agreements

When an AMI product uses **Annual (Configurable Upfront) pricing**, AWS Marketplace creates **two separate agreements**:

1. **Usage-Based Agreement** — covers metered/usage-based charges
    
2. **Annual/Configurable Upfront Agreement** — covers the upfront annual commitment
    

Because of this, API clients must **orchestrate two sets of Agreement API calls** (Create + Accept) in the correct order:

- **Accept Order:** Create & Accept the **usage-based** agreement first → then Create & Accept the **configurable upfront** agreement
    
- **Cancel Order:** Send cancellation for the **configurable upfront** agreement first → then send cancellation for the **usage-based** agreement
    

---

## Workflow

---

### Step 1 — Buyer: Discover the Offer

**`GetOffer`** — `POST` to Discovery API

Retrieves the private offer details using the AWS Marketplace Discovery API, from the buyer's perspective.

---

### Step 2 — Buyer: Inspect Offer Terms

**`GetOfferTerms`** — `POST` to Discovery API

Retrieves the pricing terms associated with the offer, confirming both the usage-based and configurable upfront terms are present.

Use the agreementProposalId from GetOffer response payload and ids for step 3.

---

### Step 3 — Buyer: Create Usage-Based Agreement (1st of 2)

**`CreateAgreementRequest-usageBasedPricingTerm`** — `POST` to Agreement API

Creates the first agreement request for the **usage-based pricing term**. This must be done before the annual agreement.

---

### Step 4 — Buyer: Accept Usage-Based Agreement (1st of 2)

**`AcceptAgreementRequest-usageBasedPricingTerm`** — `POST` to Agreement API

Accepts the usage-based agreement. The usage agreement must be accepted **before** initiating the configurable upfront agreement.

---

### Step 5 — Buyer: Create Configurable Upfront Agreement (2nd of 2)

**`CreateAgreementRequest-configurableUpfrontPricingTerm`** — `POST` to Agreement API

Creates the second agreement request for the **configurable upfront (annual) pricing term**.

---

### Step 6 — Buyer: Accept Configurable Upfront Agreement (2nd of 2)

**`AcceptAgreementRequest-configurableUpfrontPricingTerm`** — `POST` to Agreement API

Accepts the configurable upfront agreement, completing the dual-agreement acceptance flow.

---

### Step 7 — Verify Active Agreements

**`SearchAgreements`** — `POST` to Agreement API

**`GetAgreementEntitlements`** — `POST` to Agreement API

Searches for active agreements and confirm both the usage-based and configurable upfront agreements are in effect.

item.description:
# Multi-Product Solution — Offer Set Procurement

## Overview

This folder covers the **buyer journey** for procuring a **multi-product solution via a private Offer Set** on AWS Marketplace. An Offer Set is a grouped collection of private offers — one per product in the solution. In this example, the offer set includes a **SaaS Contract** and a **Professional Service with FixedUpfrontPricingTerm**.

Offer Sets allow buyers to review multiple product offers together as a bundled solution, providing a complete view of all products, pricing, terms, and EULAs in one place — making it easy to assess both total solution cost and individual component costs. After acceptance, each product generates its own **separate agreement**, giving full flexibility to manage renewals, modifications, and cancellations independently.

---

## Workflow

### Phase 1 — Discovery

**Step 1:** **`GetOfferSet`** — `POST` to Discovery API

Retrieves the offer set details, including all offers bundled in the solution.

---

**Step 2:** **`GetOffer_offer_1`** — `POST` to Discovery API

Retrieves the details of the first offer (e.g., SaaS Contract) within the offer set.

---

**Step 3:** **`GetOfferTerms_offer_1`** — `POST` to Discovery API

Retrieves the pricing terms for offer 1, confirming the contract terms and pricing structure.

---

**Step 8:** **`GetOffer_offer_2`** — `POST` to Discovery API

Retrieves the details of the second offer (e.g., Professional Service) within the offer set.

---

**Step 9:** **`GetOfferTerms_offer_2`** — `POST` to Discovery API

Retrieves the pricing terms for offer 2, confirming the FixedUpfrontPricingTerm.

---

### Phase 2 — Subscribe (per offer)

**Step 4:** **`CreateAgreementRequest_offer_1`** — `POST` to Agreement API

Creates the agreement request for offer 1 (SaaS Contract).

---

**Step 5:** **`AcceptAgreementRequest_offer_1`** — `POST` to Agreement API

Accepts the agreement for offer 1, completing subscription to the first product.

---

**Step 10:** **`CreateAgreementRequest_offer_2`** — `POST` to Agreement API

Creates the agreement request for offer 2 (Professional Service).

---

**Step 11:** **`AcceptAgreementRequest_offer_2`** — `POST` to Agreement API

Accepts the agreement for offer 2, completing subscription to the second product.

---

### Phase 3 — Verify Entitlements

**Step 6 & 12:** **`SearchAgreements-offerSet`** — `POST` to Agreement API

Searches agreements by offer set ID to verify all agreements created under the offer set.

---

**Step 7 & 13:** **`SearchAgreements-product`** — `POST` to Agreement API

Searches agreements by product ID to verify entitlement status for each individual product.

---

**Step 14:** **`DescribeAgreement`** — `POST` to Agreement API

Retrieves full details of a specific agreement to confirm its status, terms, and entitlements.

# Work with the Agreement API as a buyer

An agreement is a document that binds two parties, including the proposer and the acceptor (commonly, the buyer) and defines the terms and conditions applicable between them.

Buyer creates an AgreementRequest, which generates a quote. This quote includes all relevant information, such as the estimated charges that will be incurred over the lifetime of the agreement, which is critical for the buyer's purchase decision. If the buyer is satisfied with the quote, they can accept the AgreementRequest before it expires. The Agreement is created upon acceptance of the AgreementRequest. During this process, the buyer admin or buyer persona can associate purchase order to charges. Finally, based on the terms and conditions of the active agreement, the buyer is invoiced and granted a License to use the product.

Refer for [official documenation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/work-with-agreement-api-buyer.html) for more details.

# Postman Collection Setup Guide — Buyer

This guide covers the variables needed to run the **AWS Marketplace Agreement API - Buyer** collection. This collection contains buyer-side requests only, using the **Agreement API**, **Discovery API**, and **Entitlement API**.

Postman supports two variable scopes used by this collection:

- **Environment variables** — shared across multiple collections (set in the `Agreement API Environment`)
    
- **Collection variables** — scoped to this collection only
    

---

## Environment Variables (Already Configured)

These are expected to already exist in your `Agreement API Environment`:

| Variable | Example Value |
| --- | --- |
| `aws.region` | `us-east-1` |
| `aws.service` | `aws-marketplace` |
| `aws.marketplace.service` | `aws-marketplace` |
| `_.AGREEMENT_API_ENDPOINT_PROD` | `https://agreement-marketplace.us-east-1.api.aws` |
| `DISCOVERY_API_PROD` | `https://discovery-marketplace.us-east-1.api.aws` |
| `catalog` | `AWSMarketplace` |

---

## Collection Variables You Need to Preset

### AWS Credentials (Required)

Used by the AWS SigV4 auth helper to sign requests with buyer account credentials.

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `vault:aws.access-key-buyer` | AWS access key for the buyer account |
| `vault:aws.secret-key-buyer` | AWS secret key for the buyer account |
| `vault:aws.session-token-buyer` _(optional)_ | Required only when using temporary credentials (STS, role assumption, Isengard, etc.) |

**Tip:** The `vault:` prefix tells Postman to resolve the value from your local Postman Vault. Store credentials there rather than in plain collection variables.

**When using temporary credentials** (STS / role-assumption / Isengard temporary creds): you **must** set `vault:aws.session-token-buyer`. The AWS SigV4 auth helper in Postman will automatically attach the `X-Amz-Security-Token` header when this variable is populated.

### Seed Data — "All Actions" Folder

The **All actions** folder contains standalone requests. Variables are **not** auto-populated by scripts between requests — you must preset them manually before running each request.

| Variable | Example Value | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agreementId` | `agmt-xxxxxxxxxxxxx` | Agreement ID. Used in `DescribeAgreement`, `GetAgreementTerms`, `GetAgreementEntitlements`, `CancelAgreement`, `ListAgreementCharges`, `ListAgreementPaymentRequests`, `ListAgreementCancellationRequests`, `UpdatePurchaseOrders`. |
| `agreementRequestId` | `ar-xxxxxxxxxxxxx` | Agreement request ID. Used in `AcceptAgreementRequest`. |
| `agreementProposalIdentifier` | `offer-xxxxxxxxxxxxx` | The `agreementProposalId` from `GetOffer`. Used in `CreateAgreementRequest`. |
| `agreementCancellationRequestId` | `acr-xxxxxxxxxxxxx` | Cancellation request ID. Used in `AcceptAgreementCancellationRequest`, `GetAgreementCancellationRequest`, `RejectAgreementCancellationRequest`. |
| `paymentRequestId` | `pr-xxxxxxxxxxxxx` | Payment request ID. Used in `GetAgreementPaymentRequest`, `AcceptAgreementPaymentRequest`, `RejectAgreementPaymentRequest`. |

**Note:** `agreementId`, `agreementCancellationRequestId`, `chargeId`, and `revisionId` are set by the `SearchAgreements` and `ListAgreementCharges` response scripts within this folder. If you run `SearchAgreements` first, `agreementId` will be auto-populated for subsequent requests.

## Minimum Setup to Get Started

### To run individual requests in "All Actions":

1. **AWS Credentials (buyer account)**
    
    - `vault:aws.access-key-buyer`
        
    - `vault:aws.secret-key-buyer`
        
    - `vault:aws.session-token-buyer` (only if using temporary credentials)
        
2. **Set the variable for the specific request you want to run** — e.g., `agreementId` for `DescribeAgreement`, or `agreementProposalIdentifier` for `CreateAgreementRequest`.
    

### To run an end-to-end "Use Cases" flow:

1. **AWS Credentials (buyer account)**
    
    - `vault:aws.access-key-buyer`
        
    - `vault:aws.secret-key-buyer`
        
    - `vault:aws.session-token-buyer` (only if using temporary credentials)
        
2. **Seed data** — set only what's needed for the specific use case:
    
    - `offerId` — the offer ID shared by the seller (for single-offer flows)
        
    - `offerId_1`, `offerId_2`, `offerSetId` — for multi-product procurement flow
        
    - `SaaS_product_id` — for SaaS flows that filter by product in `SearchAgreements`
        
3. **Run the requests in order** — everything else (`agreementProposalIdentifier`, `agreementId`, `agreementRequestId`, `chargeId`, `requestedTerms`, etc.) will be auto-populated by response scripts.
